limitations: Syntax is observed; resolved imports, local calls, React components and HTTP boundaries are static inferences, not runtime guarantees.

Java call targets are inferred from same-class/imported declared field types and unique name/arity. Overloads, inheritance, reflection, receiver shadowing and actual dependency injection/runtime dispatch remain unknown.
Spring literal annotation paths and class prefixes are supported; constants, composed annotations and conditional routing remain unknown. Interface routes are not propagated.
TypeScript relative imports and local tsconfig paths/baseUrl/extends/references are supported. No external config reads, package exports, Vite aliases or runtime module resolution.
Gradle/package manifests are inventoried as evidence only, never executed. No dependency graph evaluation or complete dead-code analysis.
HTTP paths follow immutable constants and restricted inert URL helpers. Environment origins, symbolic parameters and spread config overrides are unverified; arbitrary wrappers may be missed.
Hidden, dependency/build, generated directories, declaration files, environment/credential-like files and symlinks are excluded. Tracked generated code outside these rules may be included.
Feature context combines literal/CamelCase/path evidence and bounded call/import hops, not semantic reasoning. Read coverage/truncation and verify source before changes.
